BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r1.claim: Inwardly, do not treat ego, desire, this world, or the next as rival objects of devotion beside God; monotheism means severing attachment and fleeing to God, whose true fugitive finds rest with Him.
BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r1.anchor: ولا تجعلوا مع الله في المعرفة بوحدانيته إلها آخر من النفوس والهوى والدنيا والآخرة فتعبدونها بالميل إليها

BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r2.claim: The warning is against the painful distance and duality of associating anything with God in existence, for the text says He does not forgive association.
BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r2.anchor: أخوفكم أليم عقوبة البعد وعذاب الاثنينية إذا أشركتم به في الوجود فإنه لا يغفر أن يشرك به

BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r3.claim: ‘Likewise’ compares the denial of Quraysh and Arab idolaters with earlier peoples, who called every messenger a sorcerer or madman; miracles were dismissed as magic and resurrection as madness, so the Prophet should not grieve.
BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r3.anchor: أي الأمر وهو أمر الأمم السالفة بالنسبة إلى رسلهم من ما ذكر من تكذيب قريش

BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r6.claim: Inwardly, rebellious souls in every age share a satanic nature of refusal, pride, and defiance, so they reject outward prophets and inward divine inspirations alike as magic or madness; abundance, comfort, arrogance, and wealth feed their transgression.
BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r6.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن أرباب النفوس المتمردة من الأولين والآخرين مركوزة في جبلتهم طبيعة الشيطنة من التمرد

NAHHAS:v4p249/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p249/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p249/r10.claim: The kaf in كذلك can be nominative, meaning the matter is so.
NAHHAS:v4p249/r10.anchor: تكون الكاف في موضع رفع أي الأمر كذلك

NAHHAS:v4p249/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p249/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p249/r11.claim: Alternatively, the kaf is accusative: Quraysh’s predecessors acted this way, with each messenger called a magician or madman.
NAHHAS:v4p249/r11.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون في موضع نصب بمعنى كذلك فعل الذين من قبل قريش

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42/r1.claim: Just as the Prophet’s people called him a sorcerer or madman, earlier people said the same of the messengers before him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42/r1.anchor: أي كما كذبك قومك وقالوا ساحر أو مجنون كانوا من قبلك يقولون للأنبياء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p425/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p425/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p425/r1.claim: God consoles Muhammad: earlier deniers accused their messengers of sorcery or madness just as these polytheists do.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p425/r1.anchor: وكما قال لك هؤلاء المشركون، قال المكذبون الأولون لرسلهم

JISHUMI:v9p6599/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6599/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6599/r1.claim: The narratives of earlier communities provide lessons for anyone who reflects; this is why they are recounted.
JISHUMI:v9p6599/r1.anchor: وتدل على أن في قصصهم عبرة لمن تدبر، وأنه إنما ذكر ليعتبر به

NASAFI-FULL:v4p181#8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p181#8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p181#8/r1.claim: The Prophet's people behave like earlier peoples who rejected messengers and called them sorcerers or madmen, out of ignorance.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p181#8/r1.anchor: الامر مثل ذلك وذلك اشارة إلى تكذيبهم الرسول وتسميته ساحرا أو مجنونا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p181#8/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p181#8/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p181#8/r2.claim: Every earlier messenger met the same accusation from his people.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p181#8/r2.anchor: ﴿ ما أتى الذين من قبلهم ﴾ من قبل قومك ﴿ من رسول إلا قالوا ﴾ هو ﴿ ساحر أو مجنون ﴾ رموهم بالسحر أو الجنون

QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r13.claim: The repeated charge of sorcery or madness consoles Muhammad: earlier peoples made the same accusation against their messengers.
QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r13.anchor: هذا تسلية للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أي كما كذبك قومك وقالوا ساحر أو مجنون

QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r14.claim: The comparison may be accusative, meaning a warning like earlier messengers gave, or nominative, meaning the situation is likewise.
QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r14.anchor: والكاف من «كذلك» يجوز أن تكون نصبا على تقدير أنذركم إنذارا

QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r15.claim: The accusative reading threatens disobedient monotheists, while the nominative reading threatens those who associate partners with God.
QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r15.anchor: والأول تخويف لمن عصاه من الموحدين، والثاني لمن أشرك به من الملحدين.

SAMIN-DURR:51:52/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:51:52/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:51:52/r1.claim: The stronger analysis makes كذلك a predicate of an omitted subject, pointing to the previous denials and descriptions of the messenger as sorcerer or madman; ما أتى then explains it.
SAMIN-DURR:51:52/r1.anchor: أظهرهما: أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف أي: الأمر مثل ذلك. والإشارة ب " ذلك " قال الزمخشري: " إلى تكذيبهم الرسول

SAMIN-DURR:51:52/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:51:52/r2.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:51:52/r2.claim: He makes the kāf an accusative adjective for an omitted verbal noun; it cannot be governed by أتى after negative ما, although the intended comparison is meaningful with لم.
SAMIN-DURR:51:52/r2.anchor: والثاني: أن الكاف في محل نصب نعتا لمصدر محذوف، قاله مكي، ولم يبين تقديره

SAMIN-DURR:51:52/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:51:52/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:51:52/r3.claim: The implied comparison is that Quraysh denied their messenger just as earlier nations denied theirs.
SAMIN-DURR:51:52/r3.anchor: والتقدير: كذبت قريش تكذيبا مثل تكذيب الأمم السابقة رسلهم

SAMIN-DURR:51:52#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:51:52#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:51:52#2/r1.claim: إلا قالوا is circumstantial for الذين من قبلهم; من رسول is the subject of أتى, meaning each earlier messenger arrived while being called sorcerer or madman.
SAMIN-DURR:51:52#2/r1.anchor: إلا قالوا } الجملة القولية في محل نصب على الحال من { الذين من قبلهم } ، و " من رسول " فاعل " أتى

SAMIN-DURR:51:52#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:51:52#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:51:52#2/r2.claim: The pronoun in به returns to the accusation implied by قالوا; the question expresses wonder whether earlier and later generations passed the same accusation on to each other.
SAMIN-DURR:51:52#2/r2.anchor: والضمير في " به " يعود على القول المدلول عليه ب " قالوا " أي: أتواصى الأولون والآخرون بهذا القول

RAZI-FULL:v28p197/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p197/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p197/r1.claim: The verse suggests messengers were denied, raising the objection that some prophets affirmed earlier law and that Adam was not rejected; Rāzī answers that such figures were prophets following a messenger, and rejecting that messenger also rejects them.
RAZI-FULL:v28p197/r1.anchor: ومن كذب رسوله فهو مكذبه أيضا ضرورة

RAZI-FULL:v28p197/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p197/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p197/r2.claim: Rāzī says God sends messengers when people need guidance amid widespread ignorance, but does not make belief in them unavoidable, since coerced or desperate belief is not accepted.
RAZI-FULL:v28p197/r2.anchor: إن الله لا يرسل إلا عند حاجة الخلق

RAZI-FULL:v28p197/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p197/r3.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v28p197/r3.claim: Some people say whatever God decrees is good and evil lies in the created decree; fire and water benefit people but their inherent force also harms the poor.
RAZI-FULL:v28p197/r3.anchor: بعض الناس يقول : كل ما هو قضاء الله فهو خير

RAZI-FULL:v28p197/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p197/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p197/r4.claim: Rāzī concludes this theological discussion with the Sunni formula: God does what He wills and rules as He desires.
RAZI-FULL:v28p197/r4.anchor: والسنة أن نقول ( يفعل الله ما يشاء ، ويحكم ما يريد )

RAZI-FULL:v28p197/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p197/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p197/r5.claim: The wording does not say that everyone said “sorcerer or mad”; it means many, perhaps most, said it, even though some believed.
RAZI-FULL:v28p197/r5.anchor: ولما كان كثير منهم ، بل أكثرهم قائلين به

RAZI-FULL:v28p197/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p197/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p197/r6.claim: Believers are omitted because the passage consoles the Prophet over his people's rejection by reminding him that earlier peoples also rejected messengers.
RAZI-FULL:v28p197/r6.anchor: لأن المقصود التسلية وهي على التكذيب

STUDYQURAN:51:52/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:51:52/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:51:52/r1.claim: The accusation repeats the way Pharaoh and his people tried to discredit Moses.
STUDYQURAN:51:52/r1.anchor: parallels the manner in which Pharaoh and his people sought to discredit Moses in v. 39

STUDYQURAN:51:52/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:51:52/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:51:52/r2.claim: The parallel can console Muhammad by showing that earlier messengers faced the same plight.
STUDYQURAN:51:52/r2.anchor: It can be read as providing solace to the Prophet by showing him that his plight is the same as that of previous messengers

STUDYQURAN:51:52/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:51:52/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:51:52/r3.claim: It can also warn Quraysh that they will share Pharaoh's followers' fate if they reject the Prophet.
STUDYQURAN:51:52/r3.anchor: a warning to the Quraysh that the fate of Pharaoh and his followers will be their fate as well

STUDYQURAN:51:52/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:51:52/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:51:52/r4.claim: Makkans accused Muhammad of sorcery or possession, as well as other charges; other verses compare his plight to earlier prophets.
STUDYQURAN:51:52/r4.anchor: the accusation that the Prophet was a sorcerer (10:2) or one possessed (52:29) is among the many accusations

ZAJJAJ:v5p57/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p57/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p57/r4.claim: The situation is the same as before: earlier peoples also denied the messengers.
ZAJJAJ:v5p57/r4.anchor: المعنى الأمر كذلك، أي كما فعل من قبلهم في تكذيب الرسل

ZAJJAJ:v5p57/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p57/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p57/r5.claim: In saying every messenger was called a sorcerer, huwa is understood before sāḥir, so the phrase means, 'They said: this is a sorcerer.'
ZAJJAJ:v5p57/r5.anchor: أي إلا قالوا هذا ساحر، ارتفع ساحر بإضمار هو

TABATABAI:51:52-56/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:51:52-56/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:51:52-56/r1.claim: The closing section returns to the opening themes: unbelievers deny the promised resurrection, answer revelation with conflicting claims, and face warning of the promised day.
TABATABAI:51:52-56/r1.anchor: بيان مختتم السورة وفيه إرجاع الكلام إلى ما في مفتتحها من إنكارهم للبعث الموعود ومقابلتهم الرسالة بقول مختلف ثم إيعادهم باليوم الموعود

TABATABAI:51:52-56/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:51:52-56/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:51:52-56/r2.claim: Thus summarizes their prior denial and disagreement; the following clause explains the comparison.
TABATABAI:51:52-56/r2.anchor: كالتلخيص لما تقدم من إنكارهم واختلافهم في القول. وقوله

TABATABAI:51:52-56/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:51:52-56/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:51:52-56/r3.claim: No earlier community received a messenger without calling him a sorcerer or madman, explaining the recurring pattern.
TABATABAI:51:52-56/r3.anchor: ما أتى الذين من قبلهم من رسول إلا قالوا ساحر أو مجنون

TABRISI:51:52-57/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:51:52-57/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:51:52-57/r1.claim: Every earlier messenger faced the accusation that he was a crafty sorcerer or mad, his understanding obscured by madness.
TABRISI:51:52-57/r1.anchor: أي لم يأت الذين من قبلهم يعني كفار مكة من الأمم رسول

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p463#4/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p463#4/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p463#4/r1.claim: Abū Isḥāq takes likewise to mean that this is how the matter has gone: earlier nations also denied their messengers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p463#4/r1.anchor: أبو إسحاق: المعنى: الأمر كذلك. أي: كما فعل من قبلهم من الأمم في تكذيب الرسل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p463#4/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p463#4/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p463#4/r2.claim: Muqātil says the charge of being a magician or madman is what Meccan unbelievers said to Muḥammad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p463#4/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: يعني كقول كفار مكة لمحمد

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:51:52-58/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:51:52-58/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:51:52-58/r1.claim: Earlier peoples of Mecca had no messenger come without calling him a sorcerer or madman.

ASAD-NOTES:51:52/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:51:52/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:51:52/r1.claim: Asad renders the recurring accusation against earlier messengers as calling them spellbinders or madmen.
ASAD-NOTES:51:52/r1.anchor: never yet came any apostle to those who lived before their time but they said

ASAD-NOTES:51:52#n36/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:51:52#n36/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:51:52#n36/r1.claim: Asad glosses the word translated “spellbinder” literally as “sorcerer.”

ELMALILI:51:47-60#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:51:47-60#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:51:47-60#2/r14.claim: The claim that earlier peoples called messengers sorcerers or madmen consoles the Prophet by showing that his opponents repeat an old pattern.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:52/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:52/r3.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:52/r3.claim: Razi says the verse means messengers, not every prophet, and its general wording does not imply every person made these accusations.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:52/r3.anchor: 52. âyette bütün peygamberlerin değil “resul” sıfatını taşıyanların kastedildiğini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:52/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:52/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:52/r4.claim: Majnun may mean mentally ill in its common sense or, in the beliefs of that time, possessed or under a jinn's control.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:52/r4.anchor: “mecnun” kelimesini –yaygın anlamıyla– “akıl hastası, deli” şeklinde açıklamak mümkün olduğu gibi

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p515/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p515/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p515/r2.claim: Every nation treated its messenger similarly, so the Prophet should patiently continue, turn from wrongdoers, and remind those who respond; God will support him and his companions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p515/r2.anchor: the same attitude was adopted by every nation towards their respective messengers

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p519/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p519/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p519/r1.claim: The Prophet should not grieve: earlier nations treated their messengers the same way, so he is neither uniquely opposed nor negligent in his duty.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p519/r1.anchor: previous nations too have adopted the same attitude with their respective messengers

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p519/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p519/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p519/r2.claim: The accusations are stock excuses: people called messengers sorcerers when shown signs and possessed when warned of the Hereafter’s punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p519/r2.anchor: when they were warned of the punishment of the Hereafter, they were regarded as men possessed

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p519/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p519/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p519/r3.claim: Like earlier messengers, the Prophet should persevere resolutely through the opposition and fabricated stories directed at him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p519/r3.anchor: with perseverance, he should combat the circumstances he is facing the way previous messengers did so with resoluteness

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p560/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p560/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p560/r7.claim: Likewise refers to earlier peoples' denial of messengers, like current unbelievers' response.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p560/r7.anchor: كذلك: أي أمر الأمم السابقة عند مجيء الرسل إليهم، مثل الأمر من الكفار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p560/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p560/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p560/r8.claim: أو distributes the accusations: some said sorcerer, some mad, and some both; Noah's people used madness alone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p560/r8.anchor: ساحر أو مجنون: أو للتفصيل، أي قال بعض ساحر، وقال بعض مجنون،

ALUSI-FULL:v27p18#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p18#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p18#3/r1.claim: “Likewise” resumes and emphasizes the matter after intervening discussion: earlier and present rejecters speak alike about the Messenger, restating the earlier description of their discordant talk.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p18#3/r1.anchor: بعد أن تقدمت عموماأو خصوصا في قوله تعالى ( إنكم لفي قول مختلف )

ALUSI-FULL:v27p18#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p18#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p18#3/r2.claim: “Likewise” is the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning “the matter is so”; it points forward to the statement about earlier peoples and their accusations.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p18#3/r2.anchor: الأمر كذلك أي مثل ما يذكر ويأتيك خبره إشارة إلى الكلام الذي يتلوه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p18#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p18#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p18#3/r3.claim: Alusi rejects attaching “likewise” to the verb under the scope of the negative particle, or to the following speech verb; neither construction is licensed by the syntax.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p18#3/r3.anchor: ولا يجو نصبه بأتى على أنه صفة لمصدره والإشارة إلى الإتيان

ALUSI-FULL:v27p18#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p18#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p18#3/r4.claim: “Before them” refers to Quraysh's predecessors, and “a messenger” means any messenger sent by God, whom they accused of sorcery or madness.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p18#3/r4.anchor: وضمير قبلهم لقريش أي ما أتى الذين من قبل قريش

ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r1.claim: The accusation may be construed as a predicate (“he is a sorcerer”) or as two quoted alternatives; in al-Bahr, “or” divides speakers: some said sorcerer, others madman, and some both.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r1.anchor: وفي البحر هي للتفصيل أي قال بعض : ساحر وقال بعض مجنون

ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r2.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r2.claim: In response to the claim that every messenger was rejected, al-Razi says law-preserving prophets such as Joshua were prophets following an earlier messenger, not messengers themselves.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r2.anchor: وأجاب الإمام بقوله : لا نسلم أن المقرر رسول بل هو نبي

ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r3.claim: Alusi notes reports and verses indicate that law-preserving prophets were also called messengers, and this answer still leaves Adam, who was sent but not accused.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r3.anchor: وتعقب الأخبار وكذا الآيات دالة على أن المقررين رسل وأيضا يبقى الاستشكال بآدم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r4.claim: Another answer limits the verse to messengers who came directly to an existing people with a message; it excludes those who only reaffirmed an earlier law, and Adam had no community beyond Eve.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r4.anchor: المتبادر من إتيان الرسول قوما مجيئه إياهم مع عدم تبليغ غيره إياهم ما أتى به من قبله

ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r5.claim: A further proposal restricts “messenger” to descendants of Adam, thereby excluding Adam himself, but Alusi also records objections to the explanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r5.anchor: إن المراد من رسول من بني آدم فلا يدخل هو عليه السلام في ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r6.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r6.claim: Al-Razi answers that a plural attribution can mean most people rather than every individual; mentioning rejecters alone serves the passage's consolatory purpose.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r6.anchor: وأجاب الإمام بأن إسناد القول إلى ضمير الجمع إرادة الكثير

ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r7.claim: Some use the majority reading to solve the earlier objections too, but Alusi finds that reply weak; reading “those before them” as unbelievers is also unconvincing, and he urges further reflection.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19/r7.anchor: وحمل بعضهم الذين منقبلهم على الكفار ودفع به الاستشكالين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p379#4/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p379#4/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p379#4/r4.claim: As the Meccans called the Prophet a sorcerer or madman, earlier peoples called every messenger a sorcerer or madman.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p379#4/r4.anchor: أي: كما كذبك قومك وقالوا ساحر أو مجنون كذلك، {ما أتى الذين من قبلهم}

BAYDAWI-FULL:51:52-54/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:51:52-54/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:51:52-54/r1.claim: Likewise points to unbelievers' rejection and calling the Messenger a magician or madman; the following clause explains the comparison.
BAYDAWI-FULL:51:52-54/r1.anchor: أي الأمر مثل ذلك، والإشارة إلى تكذيبهم الرسول

BAYDAWI-FULL:51:52-54/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:51:52-54/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:51:52-54/r2.claim: A phrase after the negative mā cannot govern what precedes it, so the following clause cannot be made the object of the verb.
BAYDAWI-FULL:51:52-54/r2.anchor: لأن ما بعد { ما } النافية لا يعمل فيما قبلها

BIQAI-FULL:v7p287/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p287/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p287/r1.claim: The rejection of earlier messengers repeated the Quraysh pattern: messengers came from God, and at least some people in every generation called them sorcerers or madmen.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p287/r1.anchor: ولو بعضهم برضا الباقين : { ساحر أو مجنون

BIQAI-FULL:v7p287/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p287/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p287/r2.claim: The accusations arise because messengers oppose customs that people follow from desire; ‘or’ may distinguish different speakers’ accusations or express doubt, since sorcery implies cleverness while madness implies its opposite.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p287/r2.anchor: سواء كانت ( أو ) للتفصيل بأن بعضهم قال واحدا وبعضهم قال آخر

BIQAI-FULL:v7p271#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p271#2/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v7p271#2/r4.claim: Earlier peoples repeatedly accused their messengers of sorcery or madness, showing that the present deniers repeat an established pattern.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p271#2/r4.anchor: كذلك ما أتى الذين من قبلهم من رسول إلا قالوا ساحر أو مجنون

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.claim: Ḥanānik means tenderness or mercy after tenderness; an implied verb such as “show mercy” is omitted because the expression has replaced it.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.anchor: حنانيك كأنه قال تحننا بعد تحنن

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.claim: This apparent dual occurs only in an annexed construction and is fixed, like subḥāna Allāh and maʿādh Allāh.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.anchor: ولا يكون هذا مثنى إلا فى حال إضافة كما

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.claim: Al-Khalīl reads the dual as repeated mercy: each moment of blessing should continue into another, making the expression emphatic.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.anchor: الخليل رحمه الله أن معنى التثنية أنه أراد

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.speaker: طرفة بن العبد
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.claim: Ṭarafa’s verse uses ḥanānik in an appeal for repeated mercy, illustrating the expression’s use.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.anchor: الشاعر وهو طرفة بن العبد # % أبا منذر أفنيت فأستبق بعضنا % % حنانيك بعض الشر أهون من بعض

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.speaker: العرب
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.claim: Some Arabs say subḥāna Allāhi wa-ḥanānihi, meaning glorification of God and a plea for mercy; Sibawayh compares the form with rayḥānahu for provision.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.anchor: من العرب من يقول سبحان الله وحنانيه

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.claim: Labbayk and saʿdayk are fixed accusatives like subḥāna Allāh; their sense resembles the response “hearing and obedience.”
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.anchor: وأما قولك لبيك وسعديك فانتصب هذا كما انتصب سبحان الله

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.claim: Labbayk and saʿdayk mean answering again and again and complying again and again; the doubled form intensifies the response.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.speaker: العرب
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.claim: Some Arabs use the nominative forms samaʿ and ḥanān, though the verbs governing those forms are not attested; samaʿan wa-ṭāʿatan is an accusative expression of compliance.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.anchor: ومن العرب من يقول سمع وطاعة أى أمرى سمع وطاعة

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.claim: Ḥadhārīk means “let there be caution after caution,” parallel to the repeated response in labbayk and saʿdayk.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.anchor: ومثل ذلك حذاريك كأنه قال ليكن منك حذر بعد حذر

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.speaker: عبد بنى الحسحاس
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.claim: The poet’s dawālik describes reciprocal, repeated action and can function as a circumstantial expression in the line about one garment being torn after another.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.anchor: قول الشاعر وهو عبد بنى الحسحاس # % إذا شق برد شق

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.claim: The phrase ḍarban hādhā dhīka means this action after that one from each side; Sibawayh also allows a circumstantial analysis.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.anchor: ومثله أيضا # % ضربا هذا ذيك وطعنا وخضا

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.speaker: يونس
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.claim: Yūnus says labbayk is a single word in an annexed form, comparable to ʿalayk.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.claim: Al-Khalīl instead analyzes labbayk as a dual, like ḥawālayk, and cites the attested singular ḥanān as evidence.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.anchor: وزعم الخليل أنها تثنية بمنزلة حواليك لأنا سمعناهم

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.speaker: العرب
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.claim: Some Arabs say lab or ḥawālik as shortened forms; the cited lines show that labbayk is not a preposition like ʿalayk, since its governing noun cannot be stated the same way.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكحنانيككأنهقالتحننابعدتح.anchor: وبعض العرب يقول لب فيجريه مجرى أمس وغاق ولكن موضعه نصب

NASHR:v2p467/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p467/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p467/r1.claim: One closing prayer asks that the end of one's life, work, and days be best, including the day of meeting God.
NASHR:v2p467/r1.anchor: اللهم اجعل خير عمري آخره وخير عملي خواتمه وخير أيامي يوم ألقاك فيه

NASHR:v2p467/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p467/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p467/r2.claim: Another prayer asks for a pure life, a peaceful death, and a return without disgrace or exposure.
NASHR:v2p467/r2.anchor: اللهم إني أسألك عيشة نقية وميتة سوية ومردا غير مخز، ولا فاضح

NASHR:v2p467/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p467/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p467/r3.claim: A prayer seeks the best requests, success, deeds, reward, life, and death, along with firm faith, a heavy scale, accepted prayer, forgiveness, and the highest Paradise.
NASHR:v2p467/r3.anchor: اللهم إني أسألك خير المسألة وخير الدعاء وخير النجاح وخير العمل وخير الثواب وخير الحياة وخير الممات

NASHR:v2p467/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p467/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p467/r4.claim: A prayer asks for the beginnings, endings, totalities, and inner and outer aspects of good, and for the highest ranks of Paradise.
NASHR:v2p467/r4.anchor: اللهم إني أسألك فواتح الخير وخواتمه وجوامعه وأوله وآخره وباطنه وظاهره

NASHR:v2p467/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p467/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p467/r5.claim: A prayer asks for the best of what one brings and does, both hidden and public, and for the highest ranks of Paradise.
NASHR:v2p467/r5.anchor: اللهم إني أسألك خير ما آتي وخير ما أعمل وخير ما بطن وخير ما ظهر

NASHR:v2p467/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p467/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p467/r6.claim: A prayer asks God to raise one's remembrance, remove one's burden, set matters right, purify and illumine the heart, guard chastity, and forgive sins.
NASHR:v2p467/r6.anchor: اللهم إني أسألك أن ترفع ذكري وتضع وزري وتصلح أمري وتطهر قلبي

NASHR:v2p467/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p467/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p467/r7.claim: A prayer asks for blessing in hearing, sight, sustenance, soul, heart, character, family, life, death, and work, and acceptance of good deeds.
NASHR:v2p467/r7.anchor: اللهم إني أسألك أن تبارك لي في سمعي، وفي بصري، وفي رزقي، وفي روحي

NASHR:v2p467/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p467/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p467/r8.claim: A brief prayer asks for help in remembering God, thanking Him, and worshipping Him well.
NASHR:v2p467/r8.anchor: اللهم أعنا على ذكرك وشكرك وحسن عبادتك

NASHR:v2p467/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p467/r9.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p467/r9.claim: A prayer asks for good outcomes in every matter and protection from worldly disgrace and punishment in the next life.
NASHR:v2p467/r9.anchor: اللهم أحسن عاقبتنا في الأمور كلها وأجرنا من خزي الدنيا وعذاب الآخرة

NASHR:v2p467/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p467/r10.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p467/r10.claim: A prayer asks for awe, obedience, and certainty that make worldly hardships bearable; continued enjoyment of the senses and strength; victory over enemies; and protection from religious calamity, excessive worldly concern, and merciless rule.
NASHR:v2p467/r10.anchor: اللهم اقسم لنا من خشيتك ما تحول به بيننا وبين معصيتك، ومن طاعتك ما تبلغنا به جنتك

BAQILLANI:v1p24/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p24/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p24/r1.claim: If humans could compose a counterpart, earlier Arabic speeches, letters, sermons, poetry, and saj' would have supplied one; the preserved literary record contains no such precedent, showing the Qur'an has no equal.
BAQILLANI:v1p24/r1.anchor: فلما لم نرهم احتجوا عليه بكلام سابق وخطبة متقدمة ورسالة سالفة ونظم بديع ولا عارضوه به

BAQILLANI:v1p24/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p24/r2.speaker: معترض
BAQILLANI:v1p24/r2.claim: An objection says the miracle rests on the public challenge and widely transmitted failure to answer it, so proving incapacity independently would seem to diminish the challenge's role.
BAQILLANI:v1p24/r2.anchor: فإن قيل الذي بنى عليه الأمر في تثبيت معجزة القرآن أنه وقع التحدي إلى الإتيان بمثله وأنهم عجزوا عنه بعد التحدي إليه

BAQILLANI:v1p24/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p24/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p24/r3.claim: Baqillani answers that the challenge establishes proof publicly, removes doubt by making incapacity visible to all, and binds experts in eloquence through the Qur'an itself.
BAQILLANI:v1p24/r3.anchor: قيل إنما احتيج إلى التحدي لإقامة الحجة وإظهار وجه البرهان

BAQILLANI:v1p303/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p303/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p303/r1.claim: Guidance and clarification depend on the favor, completeness, and intellect God grants; the Qur'an is a light by which He guides, while those deprived of divine support cannot find a way out.
BAQILLANI:v1p303/r1.anchor: وعلى حسب ما آتى من الفضل وأعطى من الكمال والعقل

BAQILLANI:v1p303/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p303/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p303/r2.claim: The reader who understands should thank God and ask for more knowledge; a doubter should keep studying rhetoric and gain expertise until reaching the sound path.
BAQILLANI:v1p303/r2.anchor: فاحمد الله على ما رزقك من الفهم إن فهمت

BAQILLANI:v1p303/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p303/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p303/r3.claim: Arabic fluency does not explain rejection: opponents differed as ignorant, stubborn, envious, ungrateful, or poor in reasoning, while poets such as Labid, Ka'b, and Hassan accepted Islam; the first generation itself shone with learning and eloquence.
BAQILLANI:v1p303/r3.anchor: ولا يوسوس إليك الشيطان بأنه قد كان ممن هو أعلم منك بالعربية وأدرب منك في الفصاحة أقوام

BURHAN:v3p157/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p157/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p157/r9.claim: In the نعم construction, the specifically praised or blamed term may be omitted when context makes it clear.
BURHAN:v3p157/r9.anchor: حذف المخصوص في باب نعم & إذا علم من سياق الكلام

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r1.claim: A poem's beauty in composition comes from choosing among grammatical operations such as ordering, definiteness, ellipsis, pronoun use and repetition.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r1.anchor: قدم وأخر ، وعرف ونكر ، وحذف وأضمر ، وأعاد وكرر ، وتوخى على الجملة وجها من الوجوه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r2.claim: The opening phrase is the first element of the poem that pleases the listener.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r2.anchor: أول شيء يروقك منها قوله : ' هو المرء أبدت له الحادثات '

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r3.claim: In the line about his two dispositions, the poet makes sawdad indefinite and attaches it to those two traits.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r4.claim: The fa in the sword simile coordinates it, while the omitted subject is understood as لا محالة فهو كالسيف.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r4.anchor: وعطفه بالفاء مع حذفه المبتدأ لأن المعنى : لا محالة فهو كالسيف

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r5.claim: Repeating the comparative kaf in the sea simile gives it a deliberate parallel construction with the sword simile.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r5.anchor: ثم تكريره الكاف في قوله : ' وكالبحر ' ، ثم أن قرن إلى كل واحد من التشبيهين

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r6.claim: The poet attaches a condition with its answer to each of the two similes.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r6.anchor: أن قرن إلى كل واحد من التشبيهين شرطا جوابه فيه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r7.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r7.claim: The two conditionals are balanced by corresponding circumstantial forms, صارخا and مستثيبا.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r7.anchor: أن أخرج من كل واحد من الشرطين حالا على مثال ما أخرج من الآخر

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r8.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r8.claim: Ibrahim ibn al-Abbas's verse gains its luster by placing the adverbial إذ نبا before its governing verb تكون.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r8.anchor: تقديمه الظرف الذي هو ' إذ نبا ' على عامله الذي هو ' تكون '

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r9.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r9.claim: The poem uses تكون rather than كان, a grammatical choice that contributes to its composition.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r9.anchor: ثم أن قال : ' تكون ' ولم يقل : ' كان '

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r10.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r10.claim: The poet leaves دهر indefinite rather than using الدهر.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r10.anchor: ثم أن نكر ' الدهر ' ولم يقل : ' فلو إذ نبا الدهر '

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r11.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r11.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r11.claim: The indefiniteness is carried through the rest of what follows in the poem.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r11.anchor: ثم أن ساق هذا التنكير في جميع ما أتى به من بعد

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r12.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r12.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r12.claim: The phrasing وأنكر صاحب is preferred in the verse over وأنكرت صاحبا.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p80/r12.anchor: ثم أن قال : ' وأنكر صاحب ' ولم يقل : وأنكرت صاحبا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p271/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p271/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p271/r1.claim: Imitation can reproduce words and the sounds of their letters, but it cannot reproduce the composition and order of meanings.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p271/r1.anchor: بل لن تعدو الحكاية الألفاظ وأجراس الحروف ، وذلك أن الحاكي هو من يأتي بمثل ما أتى به المحكي عنه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p271/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p271/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p271/r2.claim: Nazm is an act performed by the author on word meanings, like arranging varied colors to create a pattern, rather than copying sounds.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p271/r2.anchor: والنظم والترتيب في الكلام كما بينا عمل يعمله مؤلف الكلام في معاني الكلم لا في ألفاظها

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p271/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p271/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p271/r3.claim: Calling recitation an imitation of nazm absurdly makes the reciter a poet who chose the syntax and figures, and whose statements can be true or false.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p271/r3.anchor: أن يكون الراوي مستحقا لأن يوصف بأنه استعار وشبه ، وأن يجعل كالشاعر في كل ما يكون به ناظما

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p337/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p337/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p337/r1.claim: Eloquence arises from linking meanings to one another; the relation cannot be imagined between two word forms with no meanings beneath them.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p337/r1.anchor: المعنى في ضم بعضها إلى بعض ، تعليق بعضها ببعض ، وجعل بعضها بسبب من بعض

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p337/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p337/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p337/r2.claim: Syntactically compatible pairings include noun with noun and verb with noun; verb with verb and particle with particle are not compatible.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p337/r2.anchor: مؤتلف وهو الاسم مع الاسم ، والفعل مع الاسم . وغير مؤتلف وهو ما عدا ذلك

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p337/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p337/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p337/r3.claim: If relations were between sounds alone, any two words could combine because their forms do not inherently conflict; the actual limits show relations depend on meanings.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p337/r3.anchor: لكان ينبغي أن لا يختلف حالها في الائتلاف ، وأن لا يكون في الدنيا كلمتان إلا ويصح أن يأتلفا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p337/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p337/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p337/r4.claim: The author rejects those who judge eloquence only by visible word order and say a reader reciting a poem achieves the poet's eloquence as an imitator.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p337/r4.anchor: اعتمدوا في كل أمرهم على النسق الذي يرونه في الألفاظ ، وجعلوا لا يحفلون بغيره

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p276/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p276/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p276/r1.claim: The familiar account that metaphor moves a word from its original lexical meaning is misleading; examples include الأسد for brave and بحر for generous.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p276/r1.anchor: الحقيقة أن يقر اللفظ على أصله في اللغة ، والمجاز أن يزال عن موضعه ، ويستعمل في غير ما وضع له

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p276/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p276/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p276/r2.claim: In calling a brave man a lion, the speaker asserts that the man resembles a lion in courage and strength; the figurative move lies in the intended meaning.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p276/r2.anchor: لم يجعل في معنى شجاع على الإطلاق ، ولكن جعل الرجل بشجاعته أسدا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p276/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p276/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p276/r3.claim: If أسد were simply substituted for شجاع as a lexical synonym, there would be no reason for the metaphor to be more eloquent.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p276/r3.anchor: فمن أين يجب أن يكون قولنا : أسد ، أبلغ من قولنا شجاع ؟

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p276/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p276/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p276/r4.claim: Although استعارة appears to describe a word, its aim is meaning: جعلته أسدا assigns the man a lionlike quality, just as جعلته أميرا assigns office.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p276/r4.anchor: إن مآل الأمر إلى أن القصد بها إلى المعنى . يدلك على ذلك أنا نقول : جعله أسدا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p276/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p276/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p276/r5.claim: Because جعل with two objects works like صير, it assigns an attribute; it does not mean naming someone Zayd.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p276/r5.anchor: وحكم ' جعل ' إذا تعدى إلى مفعولين حكم ' صير ' ؛ فكما لا تقول : صيرته أميرا

BURHAN:v2p134/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p134/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURHAN:v2p134/r7.claim: The Prophet said every messenger bringing his message faced hostility; the sūra confirms that earlier peoples likewise called messengers sorcerers or madmen.
BURHAN:v2p134/r7.anchor: وكذلك قوله لم يأت أحد بما جئت به إلا عودى من قوله تعالى

BURHAN:v3p135/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p135/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p135/r6.claim: In these reports of opponents' words, the subject pronoun he is omitted before the predicate or accusation.

BURHAN:v3p228/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p228/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p228/r8.claim: The verse offers the strongest rebuke of persistent adherence to falsehood.
BURHAN:v3p228/r8.anchor: وهذا أشد ما يكون في التقريع على التمادي في الباطل

ITQAN:v2p456/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p456/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p456/r6.claim: Aw can divide a general report into alternatives said by different groups: some called for Judaism, others Christianity, and different speakers called the messengers sorcerers or madmen.
ITQAN:v2p456/r6.anchor: والتفصيل بعد الإجمال نحو ﴿ وقالوا كونوا هودا أو نصارى تهتدوا ﴾

RUMMANI:v1p108/r9.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p108/r9.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p108/r9.claim: The repeated accusation that messengers are sorcerers or madmen, despite generations of the same rejection, is the strongest rebuke for persisting in falsehood.
RUMMANI:v1p108/r9.anchor: وهذا أشد ما يكون في التقريع من أجل التمادي في الأباطيل
